questions.statement: Which sentence uses the present continuous correctly?
questions.context: Present continuous, San Juan, grado 11, W02.

options.text: She is studying for the biology test right now.
options.feedback: Correct. 'Am, is' or 'are' followed by the -ing form makes the present continuous, and 'right now' confirms that the action is in progress.

options.text: She study for the biology test right now.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Without the auxiliary 'is' the sentence stays in the present simple, and 'right now' requires the progressive.

options.text: She is study for the biology test right now.
options.feedback: Incorrect. After 'is' you need the -ing form 'studying', not the base form of the verb.

options.text: She studying for the biology test right now.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The auxiliary is missing entirely, and the -ing form never replaces the auxiliary verb in this unit.

questions.explanation:
El presente continuo se forma con el verbo 'to be' en presente mas el gerundio. Sirve para acciones que estan ocurriendo ahora mismo o que estan de forma temporal. Reconocer los marcadores 'now', 'currently' o 'at the moment' es la via rapida para identificar el tiempo verbal.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'They ____ (wait) for the bus in Caguas.'
questions.context: Present continuous with the verb to be, Ponce, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Is' agrees with he, she or it, not with 'they', which is plural in this sentence.
Incorrect. 'Waits' is present simple and describes a routine, while waiting for the bus is a one-off situation.
Correct. With the plural subject 'they' the verb 'to be' is 'are', and the -ing form 'waiting' completes the progressive.
Incorrect. This is the base form with no -ing and no auxiliary, so the sentence does not express an action in progress.

questions.explanation:
En el presente continuo el auxiliar y el gerundio deben concordar con el sujeto. Es el error mas comun de la unidad: escribir 'is waiting' con 'they' o 'are waiting' con 'he'. Revisar siempre el sujeto antes de conjugar.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct negative form: 'He ____ (not / read) the newspaper at the moment.'
questions.context: Present continuous negatives, Carolina, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Don't' belongs to the present simple, not the progressive, and 'at the moment' also calls for the continuous.
Correct. The negative of the present continuous is formed with the auxiliary 'is' plus 'not', and the -ing form does not change.
Incorrect. After 'is' the verb takes the -ing form, never its base form as it appears here.
Incorrect. The auxiliary 'to be' is missing and the verb keeps its present simple ending, mixing two tenses in a single sentence.

questions.explanation:
El negativo del presente continuo sigue el mismo esquema que el afirmativo: auxiliar 'to be' mas 'not' mas gerundio. La forma contracta mas frecuente es "isn't, aren't" y "am not" aunque tambien se admite la forma completa.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question is correct?
questions.context: Present continuous questions, Bayamon, grado 11, W02.

options.text: Do you use the library room now?
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Do' forms present simple questions, and 'now' calls for an action in progress.

options.text: Are you use the library room now?
options.feedback: Incorrect. The main verb stays in its base form after 'are', which is wrong in the progressive.

options.text: You are using the library room now?
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is not question word order: the auxiliary must open the sentence before the subject.

options.text: Are you using the library room now?
options.feedback: Correct. A progressive question inverts the order to auxiliary, subject and -ing form, with 'are' for the subject 'you'.

questions.explanation:
Para preguntar por lo que esta pasando se invierte el orden del presente continuo: el auxiliar 'to be' abre la frase, luego va el sujeto y despues el gerundio. El gerundio nunca lleva auxiliar al final.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which is the correct gerund form of the verb 'to run'?
questions.context: Present continuous spelling, Arecibo, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Dropping the final -e produces a misspelled form, and that is the typical mistake when forming the -ing form.
Incorrect. 'Run' already ends in -n and the consonant is not doubled, because it is only doubled after a short stressed vowel.
Incorrect. The -e doesn't change into another vowel or move: it is simply dropped before adding -ing.
Correct. When the verb ends in a vowel plus -e, the -e is dropped and -ing is added, except in cases like 'to be'.

questions.explanation:
Hay tres reglas para formar el gerundio. Si el verbo termina en -e se quita la -e, si termina en vocal breve tensa se duplica la consonante final, y en los demas casos se añade -ing directamente. 'To be' da 'being' y es la excepcion a la primera regla.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which is the correct gerund form of the verb 'to swim'?
questions.context: Present continuous spelling, Humacao, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect. With a short stressed vowel, the final -m must be doubled, because a single one produces an incorrect syllable.
Correct. 'Swim' ends in a short stressed vowel plus -m, and in that case the final consonant is doubled before -ing.
Incorrect. The consonant can't be separated with a space: the word is a single syllabic unit.
Incorrect. 'Swum' is a past simple form, not the base to which the -ing ending is added.

questions.explanation:
La duplicacion de la consonante ocurre tras vocal breve tensa, como en 'swim', 'run', 'sit' o 'begin'. El objetivo es que la palabra conserve dos sílabas en el gerundio. Si el sonido ya es largo, no se duplica, como en 'open' o 'travel'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'My sister ____ (make) a cake for the party right now.'
questions.context: Present continuous with third person, Aguadilla, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Correct. The subject is third person singular, so the auxiliary is 'is' followed by the -ing form 'making'.
Incorrect. 'Are' goes with a plural subject, and 'my sister' is singular in this sentence.
Incorrect. The main verb must be in the -ing form after the auxiliary, not in its base form.
Incorrect. 'Makes' is present simple, and the time marker 'right now' calls for the progressive.

questions.explanation:
El presente continuo tiene el mismo auxiliar que el presente simple: 'am', 'is' o 'are' segun el sujeto. Lo que cambia es el verbo principal, que siempre pasa a gerundio. Revisar la concordancia del auxiliar es la mitad del trabajo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'I ____ (study) for the test at the moment.'
questions.context: Present continuous with the verb to be, Guayanilla, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Is' is used with he, she or it, and the subject of this sentence is first person singular.
Incorrect. After 'am' the verb takes the -ing form, not the base form 'study'.
Correct. With the subject 'I' the auxiliary is 'am', and the -ing form 'studying' completes the progressive structure.
Incorrect. The base form alone describes a routine and doesn't fit the expression 'at the moment'.

questions.explanation:
La conjugacion de 'to be' en presente es I am, you are, he, she e it is, y nosotros, ustedes y ellos son are. Solo el auxiliar cambia de forma; el gerundio del verbo principal se mantiene igual en todas las personas.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The children ____ (play) in the park every afternoon.'
questions.context: Present continuous with the verb to be, Trujillo Alto, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Is' doesn't agree with the plural subject 'the children', and that mismatch makes the sentence incorrect.
Incorrect. 'Plays' is present simple and doesn't fit the idea of an action in progress implied by the progressive.
Correct. The construction is grammatically possible, although 'every afternoon' normally calls for the present simple for a habitual routine.
Incorrect. The -ing form and the auxiliary are missing, so the sentence doesn't express the progressive action.

questions.explanation:
Hay que distinguir el uso habitual del uso actual. El presente continuo con 'every afternoon' suena poco natural porque esa expresion marca repeticion; aun asi la frase no es incorrecta si el hablante quiere decir que estan jugando en este momento. El contexto decide cual es la opcion mas natural.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct tag: 'They are coming tonight, ____?'
questions.context: Present continuous question tags, Barceloneta, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Correct. A positive statement takes a negative tag, and the tag's auxiliary is the same 'are' as in the main clause.
Incorrect. 'Isn't' is third person singular and the main clause uses 'are', so the tag must repeat that auxiliary.
Incorrect. 'Don't' belongs to the present simple, not to the present continuous used in the main clause.
Incorrect. The tag reverses the polarity but keeps the auxiliary-plus-pronoun order, not subject plus verb.

questions.explanation:
El question tag reutiliza el auxiliar de la frase principal e invierte la polaridad. En presente continuo el tag se construye con el mismo 'to be' del enunciado: 'isn't he', 'aren't they', 'am not I' en las formas contractas mas usadas.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'They ____ (lie) on the beach this afternoon.'
questions.context: Present continuous with spelling changes, Maunabo, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The correct -ing form is 'lying', and it doesn't take the -e that has been inserted here.
Incorrect. 'lain' is the past participle, and the present continuous requires the -ing form.
Incorrect. The subject is plural, so the auxiliary must be 'are', not 'is'.
Correct. The -ing form of 'to lie' is 'lying', keeping the -y, with the preceding vowel short and stressed.

questions.explanation:
Algunos verbos cambian de forma al pasar al gerundio. 'To lie' da 'lying', 'to die' da 'dying' e 'to tie' da 'tying'. En estos casos la vocal breve tensa se convierte en una vocal larga y la -y se mantiene sin duplicar la consonante.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is correct?
questions.context: Present continuous with adverbs of frequency, Yauco, grado 11, W02.

options.text: He never is late for class.
options.feedback: Incorrect. In English the negative adverb goes after the auxiliary verb, not before it.

options.text: He is never late for class.
options.feedback: Correct. 'Never' works with the present continuous, and the sentence describes a present situation, not a past routine.

options.text: He is late never for class.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The adverb 'never' goes immediately after 'is', and never at the end of the sentence.
Incorrect. A second verb form is missing, because the negative construction needs 'not' or the adverb 'never' with the auxiliary 'is'.

questions.explanation:
La negacion del presente continuo se puede hacer de dos maneras equivalentes: con el auxiliar 'not' o con adverbios como 'never', 'always' o 'often'. En ambos casos el orden es auxiliar, adverbio y gerundio, con el adverbio pegado al auxiliar.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'She ____ (teach) biology at the high school.'
questions.context: Present continuous with the verb to be, Cayey, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The -ing form has no space and doesn't keep the final -e of the base verb.
Correct. The -ing form of 'to teach' is 'teaching', with the final -e dropped before adding -ing.
Incorrect. 'Teaches' is present simple; the sentence has no time marker that forces the progressive.
Incorrect. The -t is not doubled after a long vowel like 'ea', so the correct form is 'teaching'.

questions.explanation:
Cuando el verbo termina en vocal mas -e la -e desaparece antes de -ing, como en 'teach' que da 'teaching' o 'dance' que da 'dancing'. La duplicacion de consonante se reserva para vocal breve tensa, por lo que 'teaching' lleva una sola -t.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'He ____ (write) an email to his teacher right now.'
questions.context: Present continuous with the verb to write, San Sebastian, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A verb ending in -w doesn't lose the -e before -ing, and the correct form doubles the consonant.
Incorrect. No extra -t is added: 'write' doesn't end in -t, so the -ing form doesn't have a double -t.
Incorrect. 'Writes' is present simple, whereas 'right now' describes an action that is happening.
Correct. 'Write' ends in -e and the vowel 'i' is short and stressed, so the final -w is doubled before -ing.

questions.explanation:
Los verbos terminados en -w con vocal breve tensa forman el gerundio duplicando la consonante: 'write' da 'writing'. En cambio los terminados en -e como 'dance' o 'smile' solo pierden la -e y no duplican nada. Reconocer la vocal evita confundir ambos grupos.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct form: '____ you waiting for the results?'
questions.context: Present continuous in the negative question, Camuy, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Do' belongs to the present simple and can't be followed by the -ing form 'waiting'.
Incorrect. 'Is' goes with he, she or it and doesn't agree with the subject 'you'.
Correct. With the subject 'you' the auxiliary is 'are', and the negation is already expressed by the main verb 'waiting' in the question.
Incorrect. 'Am' is used with 'I' in the first person singular, never with 'you'.

questions.explanation:
En una pregunta el auxiliar 'to be' abre la frase y decide la concordancia con el sujeto. El gerundio no lleva auxiliar propio y simplemente sigue al verbo 'to be'. Cualquier otra forma de auxiliar rompe la estructura del presente continuo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does this sentence express? 'We are meeting the teacher tomorrow at ten.'
questions.context: Present continuous with future meaning, Luquillo, grado 11, W02.

options.text: An arrangement for a future time.
options.feedback: Correct. The present continuous with future reference expresses a plan or arrangement that has already been made.

options.text: An action that is happening right now.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The marker 'tomorrow at ten' places the action in the future, so reading it as something happening right now doesn't fit the sentence.
Incorrect. Past habits are expressed with the past simple or the past continuous, not with this structure.
Incorrect. Predictions use 'will' or 'going to', whereas the present continuous announces plans that have already been decided.

questions.explanation:
El presente continuo tiene un uso especial con el futuro: un acuerdo o plan definido. Cuando hay una hora exacta y un compromiso asumido, como 'we are meeting tomorrow at ten', la frase describe algo futuro pero seguro y ya organizado.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Question: 'Are you eating lunch now?' Answer: '____'
questions.context: Present continuous in short answers, Toa Baja, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Correct. The short answer repeats the auxiliary 'to be' and the subject, and it is the expected form in the present continuous.
Incorrect. 'I eat' is present simple and doesn't repeat the auxiliary that opens the question.
Incorrect. It's a valid answer but not a short answer: the question calls for just 'Yes, I am'.
Incorrect. 'Do' answers present simple questions, not a question built with 'are'.

questions.explanation:
Las respuestas cortas siguen el mismo auxiliar que la pregunta. Si la pregunta abre con 'are', la respuesta abre con 'am' para 'I'; si abre con 'do', la respuesta abre con 'do'. Ignorar el auxiliar cambia el tiempo verbal de la respuesta.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is not natural in English?
questions.context: Present continuous with state verbs, Naguabo, grado 11, W02.

options.text: An action that is happening right now.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The marker 'tomorrow at ten' places the sentence in the future, not at this moment, so the "right now" reading is incorrect.
Incorrect. Past habits are expressed with the past simple or the past continuous, never with 'are meeting'.
Incorrect. Predictions use 'will' or 'going to'; the present continuous announces an arrangement, not a prediction.

options.text: An arrangement for a future time.
options.feedback: Correct. With a specific date and time, the present continuous announces a plan that has already been arranged, which is its most typical future use.

questions.explanation:
Ciertos verbos de estado, como 'to know', 'to love', 'to want' o 'to believe', no se usan normalmente en presente continuo. Se expresan con presente simple, porque describen una situacion permanente y no una actividad en curso.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'Look! The bus ____ (come) around the corner.'
questions.context: Present continuous with the verb to go, Hatillo, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Comes' is present simple, and the exclamation 'Look' points to something happening at this very moment.
Correct. 'Look' is the classic marker of the present continuous and signals something happening at this moment.
Incorrect. The auxiliary 'to be' is missing and the verb keeps the present simple ending, mixing two tenses.
Incorrect. 'Come' already ends in -e, so the -e is dropped and the final -m is not doubled.

questions.explanation:
Verbos como 'look', 'listen' y 'now' indican que algo esta pasando en el momento en que se habla. En esos casos el presente continuo es obligatorio, y el gerundio se forma quitando la -e final del verbo cuando existe.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct tag: 'I am not tired yet, ____?'
questions.context: Present continuous question tags, Yabucoa, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Aren't' goes with 'you' or a plural subject, and the subject of the sentence is 'I'.
Incorrect. 'Do' belongs to the present simple, not to the present continuous used in the main clause.
Correct. A negative sentence takes a positive tag, and the auxiliary 'am' is kept with 'I' as the subject.
Incorrect. 'Isn't' is third person singular and doesn't agree with the subject 'I' of the sentence.

questions.explanation:
En presente continuo el tag se construye con el mismo auxiliar de la frase principal. Con 'I' ese auxiliar es 'am', de modo que la forma contracta mas usual es "aren't I" en la afirmacion y "am I" en la negacion, que es la unica combinacion posible.
